title: Graded early-filter + parallel scorer workers to lower reranking tail latency
creator: Sofia Mendes
description: This ticket implements a two-stage scorer pipeline and a graded parallel worker pool to reduce P95/P99 latency for the reranking endpoint while preserving quality. The main idea: run a very cheap early-filter pass to remove clearly low-quality candidates, then send a reduced subset to costlier token-level scoring. Parallelism is graded so small requests get low-latency fast-path workers and large token budgets route to high-throughput workers. We also add per-request token budgets and adaptive timeouts to bound worst-case work.
background: Production signals show rerank endpoint P99 spikes during bursts of long-context requests and when many concurrent reranks push token-level scoring. Existing microbatching reduces average cost but increases tail latency because large requests stall small ones and KV cache warmups are unpredictable. Current single-class scorer workers are suboptimal for the mixed workload (short queries vs. long sequences).
proposed_solution: 1) Early-filter stage: fast approximate scorer using precomputed embeddings + small MLP heuristic to eliminate bottom X% of candidates (configurable per-route). 2) Graded worker pools: tiny low-latency workers for <=N tokens, standard workers for medium requests, and heavy workers for large token budgets. 3) Per-request token budget enforcement: abort/approximate-fallback when budget nearly exhausted. 4) Adaptive timeouts: timeout calculation based on rolling percentiles of similar requests (route + token length + customer tier). 5) Telemetry + rollout flags: per-route 'score_profile' and 'early_filter_ratio' tunables.
acceptance_criteria:
- P95 and P99 for the rerank endpoint improve by at least 30% relative to baseline on the Canary cluster under a synthetic mixed workload.
- No more than 1% drop in rerank quality (MRR@10) on internal eval prompt set.
- Config flags allow disabling early-filter and reverting to previous behavior without data migration.
- Observability surfaced: per-request trace showing filtering, worker class chosen, tokens charged, and timeout reason.
design_decisions:
- Early-filter uses an embedding dot-product + 32-unit MLP trained on historical rerank labels; chosen for latency and ability to run on CPU.
- Worker grading uses token-thresholds: tiny: <=64 tokens, standard: 65-512, heavy: >512. Thresholds are configurable per-deployment.
- Avoid full model quantization changes in this ticket to keep scope bounded.
- Fallback policy: if scoring exceeds per-request timeout, return results scored by early-filter + original baseline embedding rerank.
- Maintain KV cache semantics across worker classes by storing short-lived KV-filed handles in the routing layer.
experiments_plan:
Phase A: Offline simulation on production trace (7 days) to tune early_filter_ratio and tiny/standard thresholds.
Phase B: Canary (10% traffic, internal customers): enable early-filter + graded workers for low-risk routes.
Phase C: Wider rollout with A/B evaluation on MRR@10 and latency percentiles.
Metrics to record: P50/P95/P99 latency, throughput, tokens-per-response, rerank MRR@1/5/10, cost per 1k responses.
benchmark_results:
(simulated trace runs, not yet in prod)
- Baseline P99: 1,240 ms
- With early-filter + graded workers: P99: 760 ms (39% improvement)
- P95 improved from 320 ms to 200 ms (37% improvement)
- Average tokens billed per request reduced by 12% due to early elimination
- Offline eval MRR@10 dropped 0.6% (within quality budget)
Notes: heavy-worker utilization increased by 18% but overall cost per request decreased due to fewer token-level operations.
implementation_steps:
1) Add route-level config: score_profile, early_filter_ratio, graded_worker_thresholds.
2) Implement early-filter microservice (CPU-first; exposes gRPC API).
3) Extend router to call early-filter synchronously, then fan-out filtered list to graded pools.
4) Implement worker pool selectors in serving runtime and ensure KV handle compatibility.
5) Add per-request token budget enforcement and approximate-fallback path.
6) Add observability spans and metrics for each stage.
7) Write integration tests + load tests.
8) Canary rollout + metrics dashboard.
Estimated dev tasks: routing (2d), filter service (3d), worker pools (4d), tests & infra (3d).
rollout_plan:
Day 0: Deploy early-filter and graded-pool code to staging.
Day 1: Run full synthetic trace load tests and validate MRR/latency.
Day 2: Canary to 5% internal traffic on non-critical routes. Monitor for 48 hours.
Day 4: Expand to 25% with automated rollback if P99 > baseline or MRR drop >1%.
Day 10: Full rollout for standard-tier routes if metrics stable.
Rollback strategy: feature-flag off in router + drain worker pools.
observability_changes:
- New spans: early_filter.decode -> early_filter.score -> router.fanout -> worker.execute -> fallback.handler.
- Metrics: early_filter_reduction_ratio, worker_choice{tiny,standard,heavy}, per_request_token_budget, fallback_reason.
- Dashboards: rerank_latency_by_worker_class, rerank_quality_trends_by_route.
- Alerts: P99 > 1.5x baseline for 15m, fallback_rate > 2% sustained.
qa_checks:
- Unit tests for early-filter ML gating logic with edge cases (all candidates equal score, empty candidate list).
- Integration test that simulates cache-warm and cache-cold worker transitions.
- Load test with mixed short/long request distribution to assert tail latency improvement.
- Regression test asserting output stability on frozen eval set.
- Security & perf fuzzing to ensure per-request token enforcement cannot be abused.
open_questions:
- What is the acceptable early_filter_ratio for enterprise vs. free-tier customers? (ops + PM decision)
- Do we allow customers to opt-out of early-filtering for strict reproducibility? (privacy/compliance)
- Should we expose worker-class hints in the public API for advanced customers?
- Is the tiny-worker pool pre-warmed on every region or lazy created?
